name: Krakatoa eruption
fact: The final paroxysmal explosions were heard about 4,800 km away; tsunamis killed most of the roughly 36,000 victims.

name: Tunguska event
fact: An airburst over Siberia flattened about 2,000 km2 of forest; estimates range from 3 to 15 megatons. No human deaths are documented.

name: Halifax Explosion
fact: The munitions ship Mont-Blanc caught fire after a collision in Halifax Harbour; about 2,000 died and 9,000 were injured.

name: Oppau explosion
fact: A silo of ammonium sulphate nitrate fertiliser exploded at the BASF plant in Oppau, killing 561 and destroying much of the town.

name: Bombay Explosion
fact: The cargo ship Fort Stikine, carrying munitions and cotton, exploded and burned in Victoria Dock, Bombay; around 800 died.

name: Port Chicago disaster
fact: Ammunition detonated while two ships were loaded at the Port Chicago naval magazine, California, killing 320 people.

name: Trinity test
fact: First detonation of a nuclear device, a plutonium implosion test at the Alamogordo range, New Mexico.

name: Hiroshima
fact: Uranium gun-type bomb "Little Boy" detonated about 600 m above the city; an estimated 90,000-166,000 died by the end of 1945.

name: Nagasaki
fact: Plutonium implosion bomb "Fat Man" detonated about 500 m above Urakami valley; an estimated 60,000-80,000 died by the end of 1945.

name: Sikhote-Alin meteorite
fact: An iron meteoroid broke up over the Sikhote-Alin mountains, Russia, forming over 100 craters; about 23 tonnes of fragments were recovered.

name: Texas City disaster
fact: Ammonium nitrate aboard the freighter Grandcamp ignited in Texas City harbour, the deadliest industrial accident in US history.

name: RDS-1 (First Lightning)
fact: First Soviet nuclear test, a plutonium implosion device fired at the Semipalatinsk test site, Kazakhstan.

name: Ivy Mike
fact: First full-scale thermonuclear (hydrogen bomb) test; it vaporised the islet of Elugelab in Enewetak Atoll.

name: Castle Bravo
fact: US thermonuclear test at Bikini Atoll that yielded about 2.5 times the prediction; fallout reached inhabited atolls and a Japanese fishing boat.

name: Kyshtym disaster
fact: A waste-storage tank exploded at the Mayak plutonium plant, Russia, contaminating a large area; more than 10,000 people were evacuated.

name: Tsar Bomba
fact: The most powerful nuclear device ever detonated, airdropped over Novaya Zemlya; the flash was visible about 1,000 km away.

name: Starfish Prime
fact: High-altitude test about 400 km above the Pacific; its electromagnetic pulse damaged electronics in Hawaii and disabled several satellites.

name: Project 596
fact: First Chinese nuclear test, a uranium-235 implosion device detonated at Lop Nur.

name: Chernobyl disaster
fact: A steam explosion during a test destroyed reactor 4 and released radioactive material across Europe; 31 died in the first weeks.

name: Piper Alpha
fact: A gas leak and explosions destroyed the North Sea oil platform Piper Alpha; 167 of the 226 aboard died.

name: Ufa train disaster
fact: Two passenger trains passing a leaking liquefied-gas pipeline near Asha, Russia, ignited the gas cloud; 575 died, many of them children.

name: AZF explosion, Toulouse
fact: About 300 tonnes of ammonium nitrate exploded at the AZF fertiliser plant, killing 31 and injuring thousands.

name: Buncefield fire
fact: A petrol tank overflow ignited at the Buncefield oil depot, England, in the largest peacetime explosion in Europe; 43 people were injured.

name: Chelyabinsk meteor
fact: A roughly 18 m asteroid exploded in the air over Russia; the shock wave broke windows across the region and injured about 1,500 people.

name: Lac-Mégantic rail disaster
fact: A runaway train of crude-oil tank cars derailed and exploded in the town centre of Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, killing 47.

name: Tianjin explosions
fact: Chemicals stored at a container terminal in the Port of Tianjin exploded twice within 30 seconds, killing 173, including 104 firefighters.

name: Bering Sea fireball
fact: A meteoroid about 10 m across exploded over the Bering Sea, the second-largest atmospheric impact recorded since 1900 after Chelyabinsk.

name: Beirut port explosion
fact: About 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate stored in the port ignited; over 218 died, 7,000 were injured and large parts of the city were damaged.

name: Hunga Tonga eruption
fact: The submarine eruption sent an atmospheric shock wave round the globe several times and a plume to about 57 km; estimates of yield vary widely.
